evidence: CancelOrderUseCase.execute: `const idStr = Array.isArray(orderId) ? orderId[0] : orderId;` followed by `if (!order) throw new Error(`Order ${idStr} not found`)`

UpdateOrderStateUseCase.execute: the same `Array.isArray(orderId) ? orderId[0] : orderId` and not-found check, plus `if (Array.isArray(newState)) { stateStr = newState[0]?.toString() || '' } else if (typeof newState === 'string')`
ListOrdersByStateUseCase.execute: the same block, `if (Array.isArray(state)) { stateStr = state[0]?.toString() || '' } else if (typeof state === 'string')`

CancelOrderUseCase releases stock (`product.releaseStock(item.quantity)`) before `order.cancel()`. UpdateOrderStateUseCase calls `order.transitionTo(stateStr as OrderStateType)` with no stock handling.
ListOrdersByStateUseCase.mapToResponse(order: any) and `(item: any)` skip the domain Order and OrderItem types

PlaceOrderUseCase calls `product.reserveStock(quantity)` and CancelOrderUseCase calls `product.releaseStock(...)`, but neither calls `productRepository.save`. Orders are always saved with `orderRepository.save(order)`.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
All five files share one concern: order and stock use cases. That part is cohesive. The unit still fails the rubric for two reasons.

1. Repeated input-parsing rule. The rule "if the value is an array, take the first element, otherwise use it as a string" is written separately in three files: CancelOrderUseCase, UpdateOrderStateUseCase and ListOrdersByStateUseCase. The same applies to looking up an order and throwing "not found", which appears in both CancelOrderUseCase and UpdateOrderStateUseCase. This parsing belongs to the HTTP layer and has leaked into the use cases, which is why their signatures take `any`.

2. One business rule lives in only one path. Releasing reserved stock when an order is cancelled is coded only in CancelOrderUseCase. UpdateOrderStateUseCase calls `order.transitionTo` with any state string, so a cancellation could go through it without the stock release.

There is also a bypass of the module's own types. ListOrdersByStateUseCase.mapToResponse takes `order: any` and `item: any` instead of the domain Order and OrderItem types.

Finally, the use cases don't treat repositories the same way. Products changed by `reserveStock` (in PlaceOrderUseCase) or `releaseStock` (in CancelOrderUseCase) are never saved through ProductRepository, while every changed Order is saved through OrderRepository.
